site: rx_search_run: the start-set skip loops (artifact.c:306, :323) + rx_L0 (:174)
observation: The start set is exactly \w, but the first atom is \b: inside a word (prev byte \w, current \w) every attempt fails at rx_L0. ~78% of t-1m bytes are \w (809,635) but only 184,595 are word starts, so ~625k of ~810k out-of-line calls to rx_match_anchored per MB do nothing but the \b test, a fail, and rx_reset_for_next_attempt.
proposed_change: Fold the leading \b into the start filter: a candidate is a \w byte whose predecessor is not \w (or pos 0). Implemented as rx_next_word_start(): if inside a word skip its \w bytes, then skip non-\w bytes.
regime: find-all over word-dense text (any subject where the start class is dense)
correctness_argument: A skipped position is either outside the start set (as before) or a \w byte after a \w byte, where rx_L0's \b is false; that attempt fails with resume_depth==0, so it pushes no frame, writes no slot, charges no step/work budget. Skipping it is unobservable, budgets included.
generality_guess: any VM artifact whose pattern starts with \b followed by a class (or a class whose complement precedes it); generally 'first assertion folded into the start filter'

observation: Both greedy spans push a give-back frame, but no give-back can succeed: a shorter \w+ leaves \w on both sides of the cursor so the following \b (rx_L3) fails; a shorter \s+ leaves an \s byte at the cursor where \1 (a non-empty \w run) must start, so rx_span_match fails at offset 0. Every failed word-start attempt pops ~len(word)+len(spaces) dead frames (~931k pops/MB on t-1m), each re-pushing, re-setting two trailed slots and undoing them.
proposed_change: Delete the two RX_PUSH give-back frames and their resume labels; the span result is final.
regime: every attempt that reaches the spans (word starts)
correctness_argument: \w and \s are disjoint and \w+ is followed by \b; \s+ is followed by a backreference whose first byte is \w. Each removed retry fails with no observable effect except a step-budget decrement and (for \1) a zero work charge; removing them only moves a step/frame give-up later (limits.md: give-ups may move later, never earlier). Default capacities are never reached either way.
generality_guess: greedy class span followed by an assertion/atom whose first-byte set is disjoint from the span class (or a \b with the span's own class): 'possessive-by-disjointness'

observation: With L2 no frame is ever pushed, yet every attempt still trails 5 slot writes (bounds check + 2 stores each) and rx_reset_for_next_attempt unwinds them after each failure. Every slot the matcher reads is written earlier in the same attempt, so the restored values are never observed.
proposed_change: On top of L2: RX_SET becomes a plain store (no trail).
correctness_argument: Trail only feeds frame resumption (none after L2) and the between-attempt reset; slots 6,4,2,3,5 are each written before being read within an attempt, and only slots 2,3 of a successful attempt are reported. A caller buffer with ntrail<5 no longer gives up with PCREC_ERR_FRAMES (give-up later, retryable per match_api 10.3).
generality_guess: any VM artifact where the trailed slots are all write-before-read within an attempt and no frame can resume

site: rx_match_anchored call from rx_search_run (asm: bl _rx_match_anchored at artifact.s:447) + rx_fail (:248-259)
observation: rx_match_anchored is out of line (it takes label addresses for the resume frames), so each attempt pays a call, spills the run state through the run pointer and reloads it. After L2/L3 the function is straight-line and rx_fail can only ever return -1.
proposed_change: L1+L2+L3, plus rx_fail reduced to 'return -1' and rx_match_anchored marked static inline always_inline.
correctness_argument: With no RX_PUSH left, resume_depth stays 0 from rx_run_state_init/rx_reset_for_next_attempt, so rx_fail's first test always returned -1; inlining changes no semantics.
generality_guess: any VM artifact whose program has no live resume frame (all spans possessive-by-disjointness)

observation: After a failed word-start attempt, L1's skip re-reads the whole word (and the whitespace) that the \w+ and \s+ spans just walked: every word byte is classified twice and each run end costs a second data-dependent loop exit (branch mispredict).
proposed_change: On top of L4: the matcher reports the furthest span cursor it proved dead (\w+ span end, then \s+ span end) through an internal out-parameter; the search loop restarts rx_next_word_start from there instead of attempt+1.
regime: failed word-start attempts (all but ~0.2% of them on t-1m)
correctness_argument: Positions strictly inside the \w+ run have a \w predecessor (\b fails); positions inside the \s+ run are \s, outside the start set. The hint is only advanced past positions so proven; default is attempt+1 (the original progression).
expected_effect: fewer bytes classified and ~1 fewer mispredict per word; scratch timing owed
generality_guess: any find-all VM artifact whose leading spans' classes exclude the start set: the 'restart after the failed span' skip (KMP-ish for class runs)

observation: Class membership is tested with a 32-byte bitmap: load, shift, mask, load, shift, mask per byte (6 ops, see artifact.s L3/L42 region). The artifact already carries a 256-byte table for the same class (rx_start_set) but uses it only in the start skip.
proposed_change: On top of L5: 256-entry one-byte tables for \w and \s; every class test is one indexed load.
correctness_argument: Tables generated from the bitmaps bit-for-bit (c -> (bm[c>>3]>>(c&7))&1); only the encoding of the same predicate changes.
expected_effect: shorter per-byte dependency chain in the span loops; small; scratch timing owed
generality_guess: every artifact with bitmap class tests in per-byte loops (256B vs 32B of rodata per class)
